title: Antiseizure medication dosing
scopeNotes: Adults; maintenance and titration only — loading doses live in the status epilepticus entries and load calculators
CRRT dosing not covered — no institutional or published source supplied; ask pharmacy
Phenobarbital not covered — no source supplied

entries.title: Levetiracetam (Keppra) — maintenance dosing

maintenance.doseText: Partial-onset (adults ≥16 y): start 500 mg q12h; may ↑ by 1000 mg/day every 2 weeks; max 3000 mg/day. JME myoclonic and PGTC: same start, titrate to 3000 mg/day
notes: Label: no evidence that >3000 mg/day adds benefit

renal.label: ESRD on dialysis
renal.doseText: 500–1000 mg q24h, plus a 250–500 mg supplemental dose after dialysis
notes: ~50% of body levetiracetam removed by a standard 4-h hemodialysis (label §12.3)

renalNotes: Label bands use CrCl normalized to BSA: CrCl (mL/min) from Cockcroft-Gault × 1.73 / BSA (m²) (§2.7)
No pediatric renal dosing in label
hepatic: No adjustment: mild–moderate PK unchanged; severe (Child-Pugh C) clearance ↓50%, mostly from reduced renal clearance (§12.3)
ivPo: IV ↔ PO 1:1: same total daily dose and frequency in both directions (§2.4–2.5)
IV: dilute in 100 mL NS, LR or D5W; give over 15 min (§2.6)
No clinical study experience with IV levetiracetam beyond 4 days (§2.1)
enteral: Tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
interactions: Unlikely to cause or be subject to PK interactions; not CYP450-dependent (§12.3)
pearls: Avoid abrupt withdrawal — risk of increased seizures and status epilepticus (§2.8)
Elderly: renally cleared — dose by renal function (§8.5)
sources: Keppra (levetiracetam) injection US prescribing information. UCB; revised 6/2025 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Lacosamide (Vimpat) — maintenance dosing

maintenance.doseText: Adults ≥17 y: start 100 mg BID; ↑ by 50 mg BID weekly; maintenance 150–200 mg BID (300–400 mg/day)
Adults ≥17 y: start 50 mg BID; ↑ by 50 mg BID weekly; maintenance 100–200 mg BID (200–400 mg/day)
notes: Adjunctive trials: >400 mg/day was not more effective and had substantially more adverse reactions

maintenance.agent: Lacosamide — alternate initial regimen (faster to maintenance)
maintenance.doseText: Adults ≥17 y: single 200 mg loading dose, then 100 mg BID starting 12 h later for 1 week; then titrate weekly if needed
notes: Give the load under medical supervision — more CNS and cardiovascular adverse reactions (§2.2)

renal.label: CrCl <30 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault) or ESRD
renal.doseText: Reduce the maximum dosage by 25% (300 mg/day if the maximum is 400 mg/day)

renal.label: Intermittent hemodialysis
renal.doseText: Effectively removed by HD; after a 4-h session consider supplementing up to 50% of the dose

renalNotes: In all renal impairment, start and titrate by response and tolerability (§2.4)
With strong CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 inhibitors, a dose reduction may be needed in renal impairment (§2.4)
hepatic: Mild or moderate: reduce the maximum dosage by 25% (§2.5)
With strong CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 inhibitors, a dose reduction may be needed in hepatic impairment (§2.5)
ivPo: IV and oral dosing are the same (§2.1)
IV over 30–60 min; adults may receive it over as little as 15 min if required (§2.7)
IV experience limited to 5 consecutive days (§2.1)
enteral: Tablets: swallow whole; do not divide (§2.6)
Oral solution may be given via NG or gastrostomy tube (§2.6)
interactions: Strong CYP3A4/CYP2C9 inhibitors: dose reduction may be needed with renal or hepatic impairment (§2.4–2.5)
Phenytoin/fosphenytoin may lower lacosamide levels (Cerebyx label Table 7)
pearls: IV can cause bradycardia, AV block and ventricular tachyarrhythmia; ECG before starting and at steady state if proarrhythmic conditions or conduction-affecting drugs (§2.7)
sources: Vimpat (lacosamide) tablets, injection, oral solution US prescribing information. UCB; revised 5/2026 (user-supplied label)
Cerebyx (fosphenytoin sodium) injection US prescribing information. Pfizer; revised 5/2025 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Brivaracetam (Briviact) — maintenance dosing

maintenance.doseText: Adults ≥16 y: 50 mg BID; adjust to 25–100 mg BID (50–200 mg/day) by response and tolerability; no titration needed

renalNotes: <10% excreted unchanged; HD not expected to enhance clearance (§10)
hepatic: All Child-Pugh classes: start 25 mg BID; max 75 mg BID (150 mg/day) (§2.5, Table 2)
ivPo: IV = PO: same dose and frequency; tablets, solution and injection interchangeable (§2.1, §12.3)
IV over 2–15 min; undiluted or in NS, LR or D5W (§2.3)
IV experience up to 4 consecutive days (§2.1)
enteral: Tablets: swallow whole; do not chew or crush (§2.2)
Oral solution may be given via NG or gastrostomy tube (§2.2)
interactions: Rifampin: increase brivaracetam dose by up to 100% (§2.6, §7.1)
Phenytoin: brivaracetam can raise phenytoin levels — monitor levels when adding or stopping (§7.3)
Carbamazepine: ↑ carbamazepine-epoxide; reduce carbamazepine if not tolerated (§7.2)
CYP2C19 poor metabolizers or CYP2C19 inhibitors may need a lower dose (§12.3)
pearls: No added benefit when combined with levetiracetam (§7.4)
Psychiatric adverse reactions (irritability, psychosis) can occur (§5.3)
sources: Briviact (brivaracetam) tablets, oral solution, injection US prescribing information. UCB; revised 4/2026 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Valproate (Depacon IV / Depakote) — maintenance dosing

maintenance.doseText: Adults and children ≥10 y: start 10–15 mg/kg/day; ↑ by 5–10 mg/kg/day weekly to response; max 60 mg/kg/day. Divide if >250 mg/day
notes: Label maximum 60 mg/kg/day (not expressible as a DoseCap — per-kg)
Elderly: lower starting dose, slower titration (§2.2)
evidenceNote: Valproate sodium injection label §2.1–2.2; Depakote label §2.2

renal.label: Intermittent hemodialysis
renal.doseText: No dose adjustment per label; HD lowers valproate concentrations ~20%

renalNotes: No adjustment in renal failure; CrCl <10 mL/min: unbound clearance ↓27% (IV label §12.3)
Protein binding substantially reduced in renal failure — total levels may mislead (IV label §12.3)
hepatic: Contraindicated in hepatic disease or significant hepatic dysfunction (label §4)
Hepatic disease: free levels may be high while total looks normal (IV label §12.3)
ivPo: Oral → IV: same total daily dose, same frequency; infuse over 60 min, ≤20 mg/min (IV label §2.1)
IV–oral equivalence shown only with q6h dosing; with BID/TID IV dosing, troughs may be lower — monitor trough levels (IV label §2.1)
IV use >14 days not studied — switch to oral when feasible (IV label §2.1)
Valproic acid → Depakote: same daily dose and schedule; once stable, BID or TID may be used (Depakote §2.2)
enteral: Depakote delayed-release: swallow whole; do not crush or chew (Depakote §2.1)
Tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
levels: Thrombocytopenia risk rises at total ≥110 mcg/mL (women) or ≥135 mcg/mL (men)

Free fraction rises with concentration (~10% at 40 → 18.5% at 130 mcg/mL) and is higher in elderly, hyperlipidemia, hepatic and renal disease — total level is not a reliable index of active drug (IV label §12.2–12.3)
interactions: Carbapenems (meropenem, imipenem, ertapenem): clinically significant ↓ valproate levels with loss of seizure control — monitor levels; change antibiotic or ASM if levels drop
Phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital can double valproate clearance (IV label §7.1)
Aspirin: valproate free fraction ↑ ~4-fold (IV label §7.1)
Lamotrigine: valproate more than doubles lamotrigine levels — lamotrigine dose must be reduced; ↑ serious rash risk
Phenytoin: valproate displaces phenytoin (free fraction +60% in volunteers) — use free phenytoin levels; combination ↑ hyperammonemia risk
Topiramate: hyperammonemia and encephalopathy (IV label §7.3)
pearls: Check ammonia for unexplained lethargy, vomiting or mental-status change (label §5)
Boxed warnings: hepatotoxicity, fetal risk, pancreatitis
Contraindicated with POLG mitochondrial disease and urea cycle disorders (label §4)
sources: Valproate sodium injection US prescribing information. Hikma; revised 12/2023 (user-supplied label)
Depakote (divalproex sodium) delayed-release tablets US prescribing information. AbbVie; revised 3/2026 (user-supplied label)
Lamictal (lamotrigine) tablets, tablets for oral suspension, ODT US prescribing information. GlaxoSmithKline; revised 10/2025 (user-supplied label)
Cerebyx (fosphenytoin sodium) injection US prescribing information. Pfizer; revised 5/2025 (user-supplied label)

entries.title: Phenytoin / fosphenytoin — maintenance dosing and levels

maintenance.doseText: Adult initial maintenance 4–6 mg PE/kg/day in divided doses; ≤150 mg PE/min; then individualize by levels
notes: Continuous ECG, BP and respiratory monitoring during and after IV infusion (boxed warning)

maintenance.doseText: Adults: start 100 mg TID; most need 100 mg TID–QID; max 200 mg TID. Once-daily 300 mg only with extended capsules, once controlled on 100 mg TID
Adults: start 125 mg (5 mL) TID; up to 625 mg (25 mL)/day
notes: Free acid — ~8% more phenytoin than the sodium-salt products (capsules, IV); monitor levels when switching (§2.4)

renalNotes: No renal dose table; unbound fraction ↑ in renal disease — dose and monitor by free levels (Cerebyx §2.7; Dilantin §2.5)
After IV fosphenytoin in renal/hepatic disease or hypoalbuminemia, conversion to phenytoin may outpace phenytoin clearance → more adverse events (Cerebyx §2.7)
Fosphenytoin phosphate load 0.0037 mmol/mg PE — consider in severe renal impairment (Cerebyx §5.12)
hepatic: Liver impairment: early toxicity possible; monitor unbound levels (Cerebyx §8.6)
ivPo: Oral phenytoin → fosphenytoin IV/IM: same total daily mg PE; levels may rise modestly (capsules ~90% bioavailable vs 100% IV/IM) (Cerebyx §2.6)
1 mg PE = 1 mg phenytoin sodium — no conversion between fosphenytoin and phenytoin sodium (Cerebyx §2.1, §5.1)
Suspension (free acid) ↔ capsules/IV (sodium salt): ~8% difference in drug content — monitor levels (Dilantin §2.4)
enteral: Enteral feeds lower phenytoin levels — don't give with a feed; check levels more often (Dilantin §7.4)
Tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
levels: Target 10–20 mcg/mL total; 1–2 mcg/mL free (Cerebyx §2.5; Dilantin §2.3)
Use free levels in renal or hepatic disease, hypoalbuminemia and pregnancy (Cerebyx §2.7, §2.9)
After fosphenytoin, wait ~2 h after IV (4 h after IM) to draw — immunoassays overestimate before conversion; if earlier, use EDTA tube (Cerebyx §2.5)
Steady state takes 7–10 days; don't change dose more often than every 7–10 days (Dilantin §2.3, §12.3)
Saturable metabolism: a ≥10% dose increase can raise levels disproportionately (Dilantin §12.3)
Toxicity is variable: nystagmus ~20, ataxia ~30, dysarthria/lethargy >40 mcg/mL (Cerebyx §10)
interactions: Valproate: displaces phenytoin and inhibits its metabolism — use free levels; ↑ hyperammonemia risk (Cerebyx §7.3)
Brivaracetam can raise phenytoin levels (Briviact §7.3)
Phenytoin lowers levels of apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, ticagrelor, nimodipine, lamotrigine (~40%) and lacosamide (Cerebyx Table 7; Lamictal Table 13)
TMP-SMX: ↑ phenytoin toxicity risk
Warfarin: PT/INR can rise or fall (Cerebyx Table 7)
pearls: IV contraindicated with sinus bradycardia, SA block, 2nd/3rd-degree AV block, Adams-Stokes (Cerebyx §4)
CYP2C9 *2/*3 carriers: start low and follow levels (Cerebyx §8.7)
Correction equations are estimates — see calc:phenytoin-correction; a measured free level is preferred
sources: Cerebyx (fosphenytoin sodium) injection US prescribing information. Pfizer; revised 5/2025 (user-supplied label)
Dilantin (extended phenytoin sodium capsules) US prescribing information. Viatris; revised 8/2023 (DailyMed setid 86dd27d1-9cee-48ae-b55d-e2d2f7dbc593, accessed 2026-11-06)

entries.title: Lamotrigine (Lamictal) — titration

maintenance.doseText: Wk 1–2: 25 mg every other day. Wk 3–4: 25 mg daily. Then ↑ 25–50 mg/day every 1–2 wk. Usual maintenance 100–200 mg/day (valproate alone) or 100–400 mg/day (valproate + inducers), in 1–2 doses
Wk 1–2: 25 mg daily. Wk 3–4: 50 mg daily. Then ↑ 50 mg/day every 1–2 wk. Usual maintenance 225–375 mg/day in 2 doses

maintenance.agent: Lamotrigine — WITH carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital or primidone (no valproate)
maintenance.doseText: Wk 1–2: 50 mg/day. Wk 3–4: 100 mg/day in 2 doses. Then ↑ 100 mg/day every 1–2 wk. Usual maintenance 300–500 mg/day in 2 doses
notes: Rifampin and lopinavir/ritonavir: use this column (§2.2)

renal.label: Intermittent hemodialysis
renal.doseText: No supplemental dose stated; ~20% of body lamotrigine removed per 4-h session (§12.3)

renalNotes: Start per concomitant medications; reduced maintenance doses may be effective in significant renal impairment; little experience in severe impairment — use caution (§2.1, §8.7)
Half-life roughly doubles in chronic renal failure (§8.7)
hepatic: Moderate or severe without ascites: reduce initial, escalation and maintenance doses by ~25% (§2.1)
ivPo: Oral only — no parenteral formulation in label (§3)
enteral: Tablets for oral suspension: swallow whole, chew, or disperse in a small amount of water or diluted juice and take all of it (§2.5)
ODT: place on tongue; with or without water (§2.6)
Tube administration not addressed in label — confirm with pharmacy
levels: No established therapeutic range — dose by response; levels may help with interacting drugs (§2.1, §5.14)
interactions: Valproate: lamotrigine levels ↑ slightly more than 2-fold (Table 13)
Carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital/primidone, rifampin: lamotrigine ↓ ~40% (Table 13)
Estrogen-containing OCs: lamotrigine ↓ ~50%; maintenance often needs up to 2×; levels rise in the pill-free week (§2.1, §5.9)
Lopinavir/ritonavir ↓ ~50%; atazanavir/ritonavir ↓ ~32% (Table 13)
Avoid OCT2 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index (e.g., dofetilide) (§7)
pearls: Serious rash risk ↑ with valproate, exceeding the initial dose or escalation, HLA-B*1502; most within 2–8 weeks; stop at first rash unless clearly not drug-related (boxed warning)
Off >5 half-lives: restart with the initial titration; don't restart after lamotrigine rash unless benefit clearly outweighs risk (§2.1)
Class IB antiarrhythmic activity in vitro — weigh risk in structural/functional heart disease (§5.4)
Can cause false-positive PCP on rapid urine drug screens (§5.14)
Taper over ≥2 weeks (~50%/week) unless safety requires faster (§2.1)
sources: Lamictal (lamotrigine) tablets, tablets for oral suspension, ODT US prescribing information. GlaxoSmithKline; revised 10/2025 (user-supplied label)
